3	My [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) config: an Orca-style window built from Herdr's layouts and mods.
4	
5	- **Orca**: the `orca` layout (`layouts/orca.json`) and the `orca-*` mods are a re-creation of Orca's UI in Herdr.
6	- **skillshare**: the right sidebar icon opens the skillshare panel (`mods/skillshare/`, a mod this repo owns). Its CLI is also required for data and actions.
7	- **Usage**: the bottom bar shows Claude, Codex and opencode usage (`orca-status/`). Claude and
8	  Codex read what the CLIs already write on this computer; Claude's quota comes live from
9	  Claude Code's own `rate_limits` statusline feed, with Anthropic's usage API only as the idle
10	  fallback (its token is read from the macOS Keychain and never written anywhere). Cached in
11	  `~/.cache/herdr-usage/`.
12	- **Follow into a worktree**: an agent CLI that takes its own process into a linked git worktree
13	  (`claude --worktree`, `codex --worktree`, or a `cd` inside the CLI) takes its tab with it: the
14	  tab moves into that worktree's space, so the sidebar lists it under the branch, and the agent
15	  keeps running (`terminal.park` → `terminal.keep`, no restart). A space left without tabs gets
16	  one, a named tab keeps its name, and the window only follows when the moved tab was on screen.
17	  The watcher is `orca-status/wt-follow.js` in the always-mounted bottom bar: it reads each agent's
18	  own process folder (`hc get` → `foreground.cwd`) and polls every 3 s.
19	- **Custom**: `orca-new-menu` (the "Start an agent" menu with the `>` setup flyout), `agent-config` (model and effort chooser, cached per CLI version), `orca-tabs` and `orca-panel-gap` changes.
20	- **Refresh branches**: the Projects header's Workspace options popup starts with it. It asks
21	  `orca-spaces` (`orca-spaces.refresh`) to re-read every project it knows — open or closed —
22	  instead of waiting for the 60-second fallback or a filesystem wake: each project's branch and
23	  its `git worktree list`, so a checkout or worktree changed elsewhere shows up. Rows are still
24	  worktrees, as in Orca, so a branch with no checkout (say `main` while the main checkout sits on
25	  a feature branch) has no card; only a space of its own brings one.
26	- **Checkout branch**: a card's right-click menu has Checkout branch, which lists the repo's local
27	  branches and runs `git switch` in that checkout. Orca switches from its Source Control panel,
28	  which this layout does not port, so the dialog ports that picker's rules instead: the current
29	  branch and a branch another worktree holds are not offered, and a working agent or uncommitted
30	  changes stop the switch with the reason shown (Git is re-checked on every attempt). The card's
31	  branch follows the switch, so returning the main checkout to `main` after a merge needs no
32	  terminal.
33	- **Agent Manager**: the sidebar's bottom Agents button opens a Settings-style page with separately scrollable Installed and Available to install groups, each showing up to
34	  5.5 rows. It lists the Agent CLIs Herdr detects,
35	  turns availability on/off for installed CLIs, and edits each CLI's executable and launch
36	  arguments. Commands are written to `programs.json`; the on/off choice lives in
37	  `agent-manager.json`. Refresh re-checks this computer by running a login-shell `command -v`
38	  probe, because `knownAgents()` caches for a minute and offers no force option.
39	- **Permissions**: a Permissions card on the same page sets how much every agent may do without
40	  asking — Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access, or each agent's own settings — and each
41	  agent row has its own permission menu beside the command. The choice is stored in
42	  `agent-manager.json` (`permissions.default` + `permissions.overrides`) and written into
43	  `programs.json`'s `run` as that agent's flag recipe (`--permission-mode auto`,
44	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--approve-for-me`, …), so every launcher honors it. Agents
45	  that have no permission flag stay on their own settings, and a command that sets unfamiliar
46	  permission flags shows as Custom and is never rewritten by an all-agents change.
47	- **Install/uninstall**: Install opens the official guide for the user to follow. Uninstall is
48	  only automated when the executable belongs to its verified npm-global package; it asks for
49	  confirmation, refuses while a live session uses it, and never touches settings, sessions or
50	  command overrides.
51	- **Start an agent**: the Orca menu shows only installed and enabled official agents. Disabled and
52	  uninstalled entries are absent, not greyed out. When nothing official and no FreeBuff is
53	  available it shows one **Open Agent Settings** action. FreeBuff is the only unofficial row and
54	  appears only when its executable is detected, with an Unofficial divider.

56	## How the quota bar gets its numbers
57	
58	Same core as Orca desktop (MIT, Lovecast Inc.), read from its public source:
59	
60	- **Claude, live.** Claude Code hands its `statusLine` command a JSON payload on every turn;
61	  that payload includes the 5-hour and weekly `rate_limits` the Messages API returned, so it
62	  costs no extra request and no usage-endpoint budget. Orca's script forwards it to a local
63	  server. Herdr has none, so `orca-status/claude-statusline.sh` writes the same windows to
64	  `~/.cache/herdr-usage/claude-statusline.json` and then runs the status line you already had.
65	  Every Claude session shares that one file, and each reports from its own last response, so the
66	  wrapper merges per window — newer `resets_at` wins, and inside one window the larger
67	  percentage wins — instead of letting the last writer (often a quiet pane still on an old
68	  number) replace the pane you are watching.
69	- **Claude, idle fallback.** When no session has changed the windows for 5 minutes, the bar polls
70	  `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` (15-minute cache) for the same windows plus per-model
71	  pools such as Fable.
72	- **Codex.** Codex appends `token_count`/`rate_limits` to its session JSONL every turn; the bar
73	  reads the newest session that has them. (Orca gets the same values from `codex app-server`'s
74	  `account/rateLimits/read`, the chatgpt.com backend, or a hidden `/status` PTY when those fail.)
75	- **opencode.** Its SQLite database, tokens since the daily reset.
76	
77	Herdr mods cannot receive a process's output directly, so the push channel is the folder that
78	process writes into: `watchFolder` wakes the bar the moment Claude, Codex or opencode write
79	(`main.js`), with a 5-minute timer only as a fallback for a missing folder and the idle OAuth
80	refresh.
81	
82	To enable the live Claude feed, point `statusLine` in `~/.claude/settings.json` at the wrapper:
83	
84	```json
85	{
86	  "statusLine": {
87	    "type": "command",
88	    "command": "sh ~/.config/herdr-app/mods/orca-status/claude-statusline.sh"
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	The wrapper passes the payload on to `$HERDR_STATUSLINE`, then `ccstatusline` from `PATH`, then
94	`npx -y ccstatusline@latest`, so the status line you see does not change.
95	
96	## How the repo is organized
97	
98	- The repo holds only our own mods (`orca-*`, `agent-config`, and `skillshare`, which this repo
99	  owns even though it wraps a local CLI). Herdr ships its own mods and layouts (`confirm`,
100	  `picker`, `main`, `terminals`, …); they stay in the live config and are not tracked here.
101	- Orca UI starts at [orca-ui/app.mjs](orca-ui/app.mjs): a reading map that lists each migrated
102	  feature, the screen it draws and the files to follow next. A feature is edited in
103	  `orca-ui/features/<area>/<feature>/` and regenerated with
104	  `node scripts/build-orca-ui.mjs --out .`. Its `manifest.json` lists every managed output, test,
105	  layout slot and key section, so the copy under `mods/` is delivery format, not an edit location.
106	  `node scripts/build-orca-ui.mjs --check --out .` reports drift and undeclared files in a feature's
107	  mod folder. A build stops, writing nothing, when a copy that differs is newer than its source
108	  (a likely hand edit, or a fresh `git checkout`); compare, then rerun with `--force` to overwrite.
109	  Run `--check` before you start editing to find existing drift. Anything no manifest lists is
110	  still edited in place.
111	- On a Herdr error (`herdr-app check`, `status`, or the window's Copy details), do not open the
112	  `mods/` file it names: `herdr-app check mods/<mod> 2>&1 | node scripts/where-error.mjs` prints the
113	  file and line to edit (a shared copy has the same line numbers as its source in
114	  [orca-ui/shared/](orca-ui/shared/)), plus the feature, tests, layouts and `next` hint that own it.
115	- A mod may import only files inside its own folder: `../x.js` and symlinks fail
116	  `herdr-app check`. Code several mods need lives in [orca-ui/shared/](orca-ui/shared/); its
117	  `manifest.json` lists the mods each helper is copied into, and the same builder writes the copies
118	  with a generated-file line as the last line, so error line numbers match the source. `--check`
119	  (and a test) fails on drift. Edit only the file in `orca-ui/shared/`, never a copy. Asset paths
120	  such as `mods/<other>/x.svg` may cross folders.
121	- Big mods are split into pure logic files, each with its own test (for example
122	  `orca-agent-manager/{util,parts,views}.js`, `orca-spaces/{storage,cards}.js`,
123	  `orca-tabs/{drop-zone,tab-title}.js`). `scripts/gpui-stub-loader.mjs` stubs `gpui-kit`,
124	  `gpui-base` and `herdr`, so `render.test.js` renders the real `main.js` and compares it with
125	  `render.snap.json` (delete the snapshot to re-record after an intended view change).
126	- Live config is `~/.config/herdr-app`; changes are copied file by file, never mirrored
127	  (see [.agents/skills/herdr-app-dev-sync/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/herdr-app-dev-sync/SKILL.md)).
128	- Checks: `node --test mods scripts orca-ui/features`, `herdr-app check <mod>`, `herdr-app status`,
129	  `node scripts/build-orca-ui.mjs --check --out .`.
130	- Not used: a bundler. Measured on two sample mods with Vite+, source maps doubled the output and
131	  herdr-app 0.1.17 ignores them, so errors would name bundle lines.
132	
133	## Setup
134	
135	Read ~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md, then add this layout: https://github.com/TonyPythoneer/herdr-my-orca/tree/main
136	
137	In short: copy `layouts/`, `mods/`, `programs.json`, `keys.json`, `settings.json` and `themes/` into `~/.config/herdr-app/`, then switch to the `orca` layout.
138

140	
141	These are runtime state or files Herdr writes itself, so they are not in this repo:
142	
143	- `data/`, `view.json`, `shared.json`, `seen.json`, `installed.json`, `window.json`, `agent-config.json` (the model cache)
144	- `layouts/.state/` (saved clicks), `icons/`, `frame/`, `avatars/`, `telemetry/`
145	- `AGENTS.md` (Herdr's own documentation), `*.d.ts`, `jsconfig.json`, `*.bak*`
146

148
